messages:
maya: FYI - AcmeCorp POC hit major issues during our 10k-qps soak. Customer reports intermittent 503s and SAML auth failures. spinning up war-room now.
chris: on it. can you drop the failing request id / sample logs?
maya: here's one: 
```
[2026-06-01T14:12:03Z] ERROR request_id=abcd-1234 model_call status=503 backend=runtime-node-7 message=\"kv cache overflow\"
[2026-06-01T14:12:04Z] WARN request_id=abcd-1234 auth status=401 saml_callback=timeout
```
sam: seeing the 503 pattern on the swarm nodes too. CPU/GPU look OK but the runtime logs show repeated "KV cache overflow" and then a retry storm.
alex: is this the same workload we saw in the replay? long prefix, many parallel chat sessions?
maya: yes - multi-tenant demo, 60-token prefixes + 10 concurrent calls per user. We pushed config to use prefix caching but maybe eviction is thrashing.
chris: quick mitigation: reduce max_concurrent_streams to 4 per connection and enable aggressive prefix-evict policy. I'll push a canary config to dedicated pool.
jen: timeline for that? customer waiting on a patch before demo at 16:00.
chris: 15m for canary roll, +5m to validate.
sam: also saw SAML callback timeouts. Looks like auth provider slowed under load, causing retries that increase pressure on runtime. Can we short-circuit failing auth to return 429 to caller instead of retrying?
alex: good call. We can add a retry budget in the client proxy (nginx/sidecar) to avoid thrash. I'll open a small config change.
maya: I'm on the customer call, they're seeing a spike of 401s followed by a flood of retries. If we can temporarily disable automatic retry on 401 -> that should reduce load.
chris: deploying canary: 
```
service: runtime-pool-dedicated
config:
  max_concurrent_streams: 4
  prefix_cache:
    eviction_policy: aggressive
  client_proxy:
    retry_on_401: false
```
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for runtime-pool-dedicated (canary id: can-6882)
sam: monitoring metrics: token throughput dropping but 503 error rate trending down after canary. auth 401 still present but less retry amplification.
maya: customer reports demo is partially unblocked, but they still see occasional auth failures. They asked about root cause and whether SAML flows are supported at scale.
chris: root cause summary draft: combined effect of auth-provider latency spikes causing client retries + large prefix cache retention leading to eviction/rehydration that produced transient KV cache saturation. Result: downstream 503s. Action items: 1) short-term: canary config (done) + disable retry on 401; 2) mid-term: implement retry budget and backoff jitter in client proxy; 3) long-term: autoscale prefix cache capacity based on active-prefix cardinality and expose quantization recommendations to sales for POC sizing.
alex: I'll write a POC runbook addendum explaining expected limits and recommended settings (concurrency, prefix lengths, retry budget). Link to draft after call.
jen: also pricing question came up: customer wants a dedicated warm pool for demo days. If we recommend higher cache capacity, that affects reserved GPU sizing. I'll coordinate with sales ops for a short-term offer.
maya: noted - please include a sample config and cost delta. Customer wants go/no-go in 24h.
chris: follow-ups: I'll open an internal ticket with logs + a reproducible replay harness. Sam, can you capture the exact metric windows for the SAML provider timeouts?
sam: on it, will attach graphs to the ticket.
maya: thanks all - staying on the call to confirm customer sees stability improvements. Will update thread with final customer decision. :thumbsup:
